lessons.title: Story Time: A Brave Explorer
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss a character's feelings during an exploration story.
success_criteria: I can say how the explorer felt.
I can find a clue that tells me.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read an explorer-themed story, modelling how to infer feelings from clues in text/pictures.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer questions about how the explorer felt at different points, using clues.
key_questions: How did the explorer feel here?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note inference skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the explorer's journey and feelings.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a time you felt brave.

lessons.title: Addition Word Problems: Explorer Supplies
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition word problems within 20.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition word problem.
I can show my working.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving a word problem about an explorer packing supplies (e.g. '6 tins of food plus 5 more, how many altogether?').
lessons.independent_task: Children solve explorer-themed addition word problems, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.plenary: Recap strategies used to solve problems.
lessons.home_link: Make up an explorer supplies word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Who Was Christopher Columbus?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall a simple fact about a significant explorer.
success_criteria: I can say who Columbus was.
I can say what he is known for.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a picture of an old sailing ship.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Tell a simplified account of Christopher Columbus's voyage.
lessons.independent_task: Children record key facts about Columbus in a simple fact file.

differentiation.support: Complete fact file with word bank

lessons.assessment_notes: Note recall of a significant historical figure — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Tell the story of Columbus's voyage to your family.

lessons.title: Explorer Routes on a Map
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to trace a simple explorer route on a world map.
success_criteria: I can find a start and end point on a map.
I can trace a simple route.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the world map and continents.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model tracing a simplified explorer route on a world map, from start to destination.
lessons.independent_task: Children trace a simple explorer route on a map outline, marking start and end.

differentiation.support: Trace with adult support, one route
differentiation.greater_depth: Trace 2+ different explorer routes and compare distances

lessons.assessment_notes: Note map-reading and route-tracing skill — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Trace a journey you've been on using a map if possible.

lessons.title: Writing an Explorer's Diary Entry
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write a simple diary entry from an explorer's viewpoint.
success_criteria: I can write what the explorer saw.
I can write in the first person ('I').
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what a diary is and why explorers kept them.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a diary entry in first person describing a day of exploring.
lessons.independent_task: Children write their own explorer diary entry (2-3 sentences).
key_questions: What did you see today, explorer?

differentiation.support: Complete sentence frames in first person

lessons.assessment_notes: Note first-person writing and imaginative detail — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share diary entries with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Write a diary entry about your day.

lessons.title: Subtraction Word Problems: Explorer Supplies
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve subtraction word problems within 20.
success_criteria: I can solve a subtraction word problem.
I can show my working.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving a word problem about supplies running out (e.g. '10 biscuits, ate 4, how many left?').
lessons.independent_task: Children solve explorer-themed subtraction word problems, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a subtraction word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Explorer Spotlight: Amelia Earhart
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall a fact about Amelia Earhart's achievements.
success_criteria: I can say what Amelia Earhart is known for.
I can say why it was significant.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a picture of an old aeroplane.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Tell a simplified account of Amelia Earhart being a pioneering female pilot.
lessons.independent_task: Children record key facts about Amelia Earhart in their fact file.
key_questions: Why was this a big achievement?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note recall and understanding of significance — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family about Amelia Earhart.

lessons.title: Hot and Cold Places Explorers Visited
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features of hot and cold places explorers travelled to.
success_criteria: I can describe a hot place.
I can describe a cold place.
lessons.starter_activity: Sort pictures into hot and cold places.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss features of polar regions and deserts that explorers famously visited.
lessons.independent_task: Children describe and draw a hot and a cold place, noting key features.
key_questions: What would you see in a cold place?
What would you see in a hot place?

differentiation.greater_depth: Compare features of both in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note geographical vocabulary use — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap features of hot and cold places.
lessons.home_link: Talk about the hottest/coldest place you've been.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Explorer Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read explorer-themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read explorer words.
I can read a sentence about exploring.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending explorer-themed words (e.g. 'map', 'ship', 'land').
lessons.independent_task: Children read explorer-themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading explorer words over the week.

lessons.title: Measuring Distance with Non-Standard Units
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to measure distance using non-standard units (footsteps, hand spans).
success_criteria: I can measure a distance in footsteps.
I can compare two distances.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how explorers measured distance long ago.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model measuring a distance using footsteps, recording the result.
lessons.independent_task: Children measure classroom/playground distances using footsteps, comparing results.

differentiation.support: Measure one short distance with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Record non-standard measurement skill — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Measure a distance at home using footsteps.

lessons.title: Explorer Spotlight: Neil Armstrong
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall a fact about Neil Armstrong's moon landing.
success_criteria: I can say what Neil Armstrong did.
I can say why it was historic.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a picture of the moon landing.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Tell a simplified account of Neil Armstrong being the first person on the moon.
lessons.independent_task: Children record key facts about Neil Armstrong in their fact file.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note recall of a significant historical event — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Look at the moon tonight and think about Neil Armstrong's journey.

lessons.title: Naming Continents Explorers Visited
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name continents visited by explorers this week.
success_criteria: I can name 2 continents.
I can find them on a map.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap continents if introduced previously, or introduce simply.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the seven continents briefly, linking to explorer journeys.
lessons.independent_task: Children label continents on a world map outline.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note early locational knowledge, building toward Week 27 — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Find a continent on a map or globe together.

lessons.title: Hot-Seating an Explorer
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer questions in role as an explorer.
success_criteria: I can answer a question as the explorer.
I can use what I've learned about them.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model hot-seating (answering questions in role) as a famous explorer.
lessons.independent_task: Children take turns hot-seating as an explorer of their choice, answering classmates' questions.
key_questions: Explorer, what was your journey like?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer unprompted, in character, with detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and factual recall in role — evidence for ENG.SL1/HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Pretend to be an explorer and tell your family about your 'journey'.

lessons.title: Comparing Numbers to 20
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare numbers to 20 using greater than/less than.
success_criteria: I can say which number is bigger.
I can use the words greater than/less than.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing pairs of numbers using greater than/less than vocabulary and symbols informally.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare pairs of numbers to 20, recording which is greater/less.

differentiation.greater_depth: Compare numbers to 20 and order 3+ numbers

lessons.assessment_notes: Record number comparison skill — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Compare two numbers at home.

lessons.title: What Makes a Good Explorer?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe qualities of a good explorer based on this week's learning.
success_criteria: I can name a quality of a good explorer.
I can give an example from this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all explorers studied this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss qualities explorers share (bravery, curiosity, determination), using this week's examples.
lessons.independent_task: Children record qualities of a good explorer with examples from the week's learning.
key_questions: What quality helped this explorer succeed?

differentiation.support: Choose from a quality word bank

lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's historical learning — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a quality you have that would make you a good explorer.

lessons.title: Making an Explorer's Map
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a simple map including key features.
success_criteria: I can draw a simple map.
I can include a key feature (land, sea, route).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating a simple imaginative map including land, sea, and a route.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own simple explorer map with labelled features.

differentiation.greater_depth: Add a compass, key and multiple labelled features

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe map-making and feature inclusion — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Draw a map of your route to school or a familiar place.

lessons.title: Explorers Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about the explorers studied this week.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question about an explorer.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage of the week's explorers, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the explorers.
key_questions: Who was the first person on the moon?
Why do you think that explorer succeeded?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress across the week's non-fiction content — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the week's explorers quiz answers.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on the explorers you learned about.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Word Problems and Comparing Numbers
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply addition/subtraction word problems and number comparison skills.
success_criteria: I can solve a word problem.
I can compare two numbers.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of word problems and number comparison.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: word problems, number comparison.
key_questions: How did you solve this problem?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 17 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/N2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising word problems over the weekend.

lessons.title: Explorers Topic Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about explorers learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name an explorer and what they did.
I can say one quality that helped them.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about explorers.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Famous Explorers' display combining fact files, maps and diary entries from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about explorers?
Who was your favourite and why?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Share your favourite explorer fact with your family.

lessons.title: Explorers and Geography: Final Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to link explorer journeys to geographical knowledge learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name a place an explorer visited.
I can find it on a map.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss linking explorer stories to the geography learned (continents, hot/cold places).
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a final map activity linking explorers to the places they visited.

differentiation.support: Link 1-2 explorers to places with support
differentiation.greater_depth: Link all explorers studied to their locations

lessons.assessment_notes: Final geography/history cross-curricular assessment for the week — evidence for GEOG.1/HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the week's explorer and geography learning.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family about an explorer and where they travelled.
